title: Lightweight Action Stream Protocol for Mobile SDKs (PRD sketch)
content:
Purpose
This is a working PRD sketch proposing a compact streaming protocol and SDK ergonomics specifically tuned for mobile clients that need tool calling, structured outputs, low-latency progressive results, and robust offline/fallback behavior. Goal is to enable high-quality, battery- and bandwidth-conscious LLM integrations on iOS/Android with minimal server-side changes to the Hosted API.

Context and problem statement
Mobile apps are an increasingly important surface for Redwood customers. Current streaming surfaces assume always-on, high-bandwidth web clients and desktop SDKs. Mobile constraints create several practical issues:
- Network variability (cellular handoffs, intermittent connectivity) causes streaming interruptions and higher perceived latency.
- Battery and memory constraints require smaller in-memory buffers and fewer long-lived connections.
- Tool calls (e.g., web search, calendar actions) must be coordinated with user permissions and local caches; naive blocking tool-calls harm UX and increase retry rates.
- Structured outputs (JSON actions, schema-constrained results) need to be delivered incrementally while remaining parseable on partial payloads.
- Developers want a small footprint SDK with clear upgrade paths and observable failure modes.

Goals
- Define a compact framing and handshake for progressive, resumable partial responses optimized for mobile (low overhead, simple parser).
- Support typed tool-calls with explicit lifecycle hooks (request -> tool proposal -> tool result -> continuation) that work with transient mobile permissions and local execution.
- Provide structured-output envelopes that allow clients to consume partial, syntactically valid fragments and recover on reconnect.
- Describe SDK ergonomics: small runtime (<200KB native), minimal threading assumptions, and adaptive back-pressure tuned to battery/network.
- Specify observability primitives (client-level events, token/byte counters, error taxonomy) to support debugging and quality monitoring.

Non-goals
- This doc does not define server-side kernel scheduling or batching algorithms (we assume existing runtime batching remains).
- Not proposing new authentication mechanisms; existing token/KMS flows used.

High-level protocol overview
1) Single connection, multiplexed light frames: The SDK opens a single connection per logical conversation (HTTP/2 or WebSocket). Messages use small typed frames (header byte + length + payload) to minimize parser overhead.
2) Handshake: On connect the client sends a compact capability vector (max bandwidth, device-class, offline-cache-id, permission-scopes). Server responds with preferred frame-size and a resume-token if resumability is enabled.
3) Progressive response frames: Three primary frame types: META (progress metadata), DELTA (incremental model tokens / text segments / structured fragments), and ACTION (tool-call proposals/results). Each frame is self-describing with a 1–2 byte type tag.
4) Structured fragments: Structured payloads are delivered as newline-delimited JSON chunks where each chunk is a valid JSON value or an explicit "fragment" wrapper. This allows incremental parsing without waiting for full document.
5) Resumability: Resume token issued per conversation; on reconnect client sends last-applied-offset and resume-token. Server can resume streaming from last confirmed continuation point or send a compact state-diff to reconcile.

Detailed framing (sketch)
- Frame format: [1 byte type][varint length][payload bytes] - small varint parser keeps overhead low.
- Types: 0x01 META, 0x02 DELTA_TEXT, 0x03 DELTA_STRUCT, 0x04 ACTION_PROPOSE, 0x05 ACTION_RESULT, 0x06 HEARTBEAT, 0x07 END.
- META: short key/value pairs (e.g., {"est_remaining_ms": 120, "model": "redwood-3b-int8"}) used to adapt UI.
- DELTA_TEXT: UTF-8 token chunk; clients append to a transcript.
- DELTA_STRUCT: newline-delimited JSON fragments; each fragment includes a monotonic fragment id. Parsers should accept missing fragments and allow later reconciliation.
- ACTION_PROPOSE: model suggests a tool call; includes tool id, minimal args, idempotency key, and a permission-surface hint.
- ACTION_RESULT: result from tool (server-executed or client-supplied) with status and optional continuation token.

Tool calling lifecycle for mobile
- Suggest vs Execute: To avoid permission/latency pitfalls, model proposals default to SUGGEST (ACTION_PROPOSE). Mobile SDK emits a local UX affordance: "Model suggests: Search web for X". Only after explicit user approval or an app-level policy will SDK emit an ACTION_EXECUTE event to server or to a local adapter.
- Local adapters: SDK exposes a small adapter interface so apps can implement local tools (calendar, contacts) without round-trip. If a tool is handled locally, client sends ACTION_RESULT back using the same frame flow so the model receives the result and continues.
- Idempotency: All tool proposals include an idempotency key; SDK persists recent keys to avoid duplicate side-effects across reconnects.

Structured output and partial parse rules
- Declarative fragments: Server emits a base schema hint in META (e.g., "schema": "todo-item-v1") and then streams DELTA_STRUCT fragments where each fragment is a full JSON value (object/array/primitive) or a wrapper {"frag_id":N,"chunk":"..."}.
- Parsers should treat each top-level fragment as a unit; when missing fragments are detected during resume, SDK requests a reconciliation snapshot (compact full object) or requests specific fragment ids.
- Validation: SDK exposes a small validator that can run lightweight checks on partial fragments and raise early UI warnings. Full schema validation deferred until end frame.

SDK ergonomics and constraints
- Binary size: Aim for native bindings <200KB (shared) + thin JS shim for cross-platform. No heavy JSON-schema libs bundled by default.
- Threading model: Single network thread, optional UI thread callbacks. Decode frames incrementally to avoid large memory spikes.
- Back-pressure/adaptive polling: SDK monitors OS network and battery hints; it reduces max in-flight tokens when on background/low-battery or low-bandwidth.
- Caching: Local cache of last N resume tokens and recent tool idempotency keys. Optional result cache for offline UX: return last-known result while reconnecting, with clear UI state that result may be stale.
- Permission handling: Tool proposals include a permissions hint; SDK exposes a standard prompt flow and a policy API for apps to auto-approve trusted tools.

Observability and telemetry
- Events to emit: connection_start, handshake_complete, frame_received(type), frame_sent(type), resume_attempt, resume_success, tool_proposed, tool_executed, partial_validation_failed, final_response_received, error_{network,parse,permission}.
- Counters: bytes_in, bytes_out, frames_received, frames_lost, resume_retries.
- Labels: device_class, network_type, sdk_version, model_id, route_id.

Rollout plan and experiments
- Canary: Implement server-side conservative support for frame types; roll mobile SDK alpha with opt-in flag in 2 internal apps. Collect telemetry for resume success rates and perceived latency.
- A/B: Compare traditional full-response HTTP streaming vs compact framed stream in apps with constrained networks (APAC) to measure token-cost, battery, and reconnection rates.
- Gate: Only enable default resume behavior after 95th percentile resume success and no critical data-loss incidents in 1 month.

Open questions / risks
- Resume semantics complexity: How far can the server reconstitute model state? We may need a small server-side protocol to snapshot conversation state efficiently.
- Security: ACTION frames increase surface for side-effects. Need to ensure idempotency + audit logs + clear permission boundaries.
- Fragmentation overhead: Newline-delimited JSON fragments trade size for parseability; impact on token accounting must be measured.

Next steps (short term)
- Engineering spike (2 engineers x 2 weeks) to prototype client frame parser and resume flow using an internal test model.
- Product / UX sketches for the tool-suggestion workflow and offline-stale result UX.
- Define telemetry dashboards and a set of prompts to drive structured-output scenarios (shopping list, calendar invite, code snippet).

Notes to reviewers
Looking for feedback on: 1) acceptable frame type set (too many vs too few), 2) resume semantics expectations, 3) mobile SDK size/feature tradeoffs, 4) permission UX for tool execution.

-- end of sketch --
